answer: An economy can resist Sybils with chained sequential work proofs: each identity must publish a proof that depends on its previous proof, like layers forming a pearl, so work cannot be parallelised. An attacker cannot simply echo one proof across many fake identities, because a copied proof fails its chain check. Creating a thousand Sybils therefore means paying for a thousand separate, time-ordered chains — as slow as cracking each walnut by hand — while an honest agent maintains only one. Idle chains lose standing, so fake identities stay costly and visible.
